title: Renewal and discovery at Kitt Peak
caption: The Milky Way above the SARA and WIYN telescopes, Kitt Peak National Observatory, Arizona
celestial: Photograph taken at Kitt Peak National Observatory, Arizona
credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/P. Horálek (Institute of Physics in Opava)

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The Milky Way rises over Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona, where few clouds, high altitude and strict limits on light pollution make the night sky ideal for stargazing. The 0.9-meter SARA Kitt Peak Telescope stands on the right, and the WIYN 3.5-meter Telescope can be seen in the distance on the left.

Kitt Peak hosts the largest collection of optical telescopes in the Northern Hemisphere and is one of the leading sites for astronomical research. This view is a close-up from a wider panorama that shows more of the observatory’s telescopes, and it doubles as an image for planetarium domes.

It was taken during NOIRLab’s 2022 expedition to all of its observing sites by Petr Horálek, one of NOIRLab’s Audiovisual Ambassadors, who has spent years photographing observatories under their skies.

understand.summary: A ground-based landscape photograph credited to CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/P. Horálek (Institute of Physics in Opava). The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera can gather light for longer than the eye, so the Milky Way looks brighter and more detailed here than it would to someone standing on site.

explore: Arizona’s dark-sky rules, which limit and shield outdoor lighting around the observatories, are part of why the Milky Way still looks like this from Kitt Peak, about an hour’s drive from Tucson.
alt: The Milky Way rising over a small white telescope dome on the right, with a larger telescope building on a distant ridge at left.
